newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Hong Kong's stock market plunged 460 points to 12,074 on Tuesday. Analysts said that with the possibility of a further rise in interest rates, the blue-chip Hang Seng Index might fall to 11,700 points.

-- China's Guangdong province announced its public security bureau would take strict measures to control mainlanders coming into Hong Kong between June 15 and July 15, the four weeks straddling the territory's handover to China at midnight on June 30.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin met Australian Prime Minister John Howard and expressed hopes of establishing a cooperative relationship based on mutual respect.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Young couples in Hong Kong queued outside the marriage registration department to book a time to wed on the last day of the colonial administration.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Special Administrative Region Executive Council had approved a consultation paper on the replacement of the Public Order Ordinance which proposed that police permission must be sought before demonstrations could take place.
-- Hong Kong's construction sector turned in another robust performance last year as contractors undertook projects worth HK$116 billion, a 16.3 percent increase from 1995.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Proposed changes to civil liberties laws would go to the provisional legislature in the form of "blue bills" before the handover, according to post-handover executive councillor Henry Tang.
